# Evidence: effect sizes and why strategy needs a test

Each rule is a hypothesis conditioned on audience, channel and barrier, not a guarantee. Read [principles.md](principles.md) for how to weigh evidence, and apply the brief fidelity, claim and compliance rules in SKILL.md first. Where an entry says a number or attribution was corrected, use the corrected form.

## 21. Small and variable effects of message design (O'Keefe & Hoeken, 2021)

- **Finding:** Reviewing 30 message variations across 1,149 studies, mean effects were small (median about r = .10) and the prediction intervals included zero, even when moderating conditions were specified.
- **Rule:** if you choose a copy strategy or structure, then justify the choice by the diagnosed audience barrier, and propose a test when a decision depends on it.
- **Apply:** Describe why a version addresses a specific barrier. Never claim it converts because it follows a named formula.
- **Pattern:** This version addresses [diagnosed barrier] with [element]; test it against [alternative] using [metric] and [guardrail].
- **Limits:** Theory generates hypotheses. Measured results in the real market decide.
- **Caveats:** The review covers message variations in persuasion research, not only advertising.
- **Evidence:** meta-analytic review; transfer to commercial copy is adjacent.
- **Citation (corrected):** O'Keefe, D. J., & Hoeken, H. (2021). Message Design Choices Don't Make Much Difference to Persuasiveness and Can't Be Counted On: Not Even When Moderating Conditions Are Specified. Frontiers in Psychology, 12, 664160. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2021.664160 The supplied base gave Frontiers in Communication 6, 686734 and a different title; corrected from the publisher record found through a web search.
